Raheem Sterling has avoided being sent to jail after he received a suspended sentence of 12 months for pleading guilty to a prolonged period of reckless driving while impaired by the drug nitrous oxide.
The former England international, who five years ago was leading the Three Lions’ charge to a European Championship final, stood expressionless in the dock as the sentence was read out by district judge Kirsty Allman at Basingstoke magistrates court.
Sterling was sentenced to 18 months in prison, reduced to 12 months, for dangerous driving on the morning of 28 May this year. He was awarded a sentence of two months for a failure to provide a specimen of blood for analysis, which is to run concurrently. He received no punishment for possession of a class C drug. Canisters in Sterling’s possession were seized and destroyed.
In sentencing, Allman found the first two offences to be of the highest levels of culpability but argued that Sterling’s charitable work, and his award of an MBE in 2021, acted as “significant and substantial” mitigation. Sterling was also commended for having voluntary submitted to addiction treatment, spending 12 days at the Banbury Lodge addiction treatment centre in June. Under the sentencing act of 2026, there is a presumption that any custodial sentence of 12 months or less be suspended.
Sterling must complete 100 hours of community service and has been banned from driving for 24 months.
Sterling was first observed behaving erratically at 1.30am on 28 May, when he was spotted inhaling from a large pink balloon while behind the wheel of his black Lamborghini Urus outside McDonald’s in Hayes. After a night without sleep, Sterling got behind the wheel again at 7.45am. Four police forces received reports concerning Sterling’s driving along the M25, M40 and M3, with one witness describing it as “absolutely horrendous”. Forced to overtake, the witness saw Sterling inhaling from a large white balloon.
On leaving the M3, the Lamborghini veered off the carriageway on the A327, crashing into the central reservation and causing “substantial damage” to the vehicle which “was no longer drivable”, according to Allman’s sentencing remarks.
Sterling complied with initial roadside breath and saliva tests, which proved negative for alcohol, cannabis and cocaine. At Basingstoke police station Sterling admitted he “had a problem with nitrous oxide” and went on to fail a preliminary impairment test. He was also asked to judge 30 seconds with his eyes closed but recorded 52. Sterling then refused to give a blood sample for further testing until he was accompanied by a lawyer.
Allman said the nature of the offences were such that she had considered the possibility of passing sentencing on to a crown court. “These offences are so serious that neither a fine nor a community order can be justified,” she said. “The custodial threshold is clearly crossed, and custody is unavoidable.”
Custody was avoided, however, after Allman took into consideration Sterling’s receipt of an MBE for services to racial equality in sport in 2021 and his ongoing commitment both to the Raheem Sterling foundation and the RS7 football academy. “I attach substantial weight to your personal mitigation,” she said.

“I further accept that nitrous oxide became a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in your career,” Allman went on. At the time of his arrest, Sterling had just completed an unsuccessful period at Feyenoord, having spent the previous six months training alone, excluded from Chelsea’s first team.
Speaking for the defence, Jason Bartfeld KC, described the incident as “extremely sad” and said for Sterling it was “a matter of his own intense personal regret” which had “tarnished his personal reputation”. Sterling left the court without making comment.

Raheem Sterling has scored 123 goals in 396 Premier League appearances and provided 65 assists
Raheem Sterling grew up a stone's throw from Wembley Stadium, and went on to start a European Championship final for England there.
At his peak, the four-time Premier League winner was earning £325,000 a week at Chelsea .
"Raheem is a huge player with a huge influence in the last few years in English football," said then Blues boss Thomas Tuchel when he signed a 27-year-old Sterling in a £50m deal in 2022.
"He is at the perfect age to take responsibility around the younger players that we have and be an example.
"He just needs to do what he did over the last few years and he will be a huge asset for us."
Sterling enjoyed a 10-year England career, also played for Liverpool , Manchester City and Arsenal , and commanded combined transfer fees of about £100m.
But his career at the top level looks to be in the balance at the age of 31 after he was handed a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, for dangerous driving. Sterling has also been disqualified from driving for two years and ordered to carry out 100 hours of unpaid work.
At an earlier hearing in September, Sterling admitted dangerous driving on a motorway before crashing a Lamborghini on 28 May.
The crash caused "substantial" damage to his car and all four wheels, which prevented him from driving further, the court heard.
Sterling also admitted possessing nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, and failing to provide a specimen for analysis.
Born in Kingston, Jamaica, he was just two when his father was shot dead.
His mother, Nadine, was determined to give her children a safer environment to live in. She moved to England to lay a path for Sterling and his sister to join her once she had found a home and finished her education, while cleaning bathrooms and changing bedsheets in hotels to earn extra money.
Sterling grew up on a housing estate in Neasden, north-west London, and spent part of his education at Vernon House, where teachers attempted to help the football-obsessed youngster with behavioural problems.
In an interview with the Players' Tribune , external in 2018, Sterling said: "I was so naughty that they kicked me out of primary school. I just didn't like to listen to anyone but my mum. That was my problem."
He was 10 when teacher Chris Beschi told him: "If you carry on the way you're going, by the time you're 17 you'll either be playing for England or in prison."
Sterling would grow to become one of the standout English attacking talents of his generation.
Raheem Sterling: From school struggles to a class of his own
On 14 November 2012 - aged 17 years and 342 days - Sterling made his England debut on the night his Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard won his 100th cap in a 4-2 defeat by Sweden in Stockholm.
Sterling would go on to make 81 more appearances for his country, scoring 20 goals.
He featured at three World Cups - 2014, 2018 and 2022 - and two European Championships. He was one of the standout players as England reached the Euro 2020 final at Wembley, where they were beaten by Italy.
Sterling was now at the peak of his career - the former Queens Park Rangers youngster, who has a tattoo on his forearm of a young boy holding a football looking up at the Wembley arch, named in the team of the tournament by Uefa.
Liverpool had signed a 15-year-old Sterling from QPR for £600,000 in February 2010.
He made his senior Reds debut two years later and became the second-youngest goalscorer in their history - behind Michael Owen - when he scored the winner against Reading in October 2012 at the age of 17.
In 2015, Sterling joined Manchester City in a deal worth up to £49m, making him the most expensive English player at the time.
He had been under contract at Anfield until 2017 but turned down a new deal to move to Liverpool 's rivals, with City boss Manuel Pellegrini describing the 20-year-old as "one of the best attacking players in world football".
Sterling went on to score 131 goals in 339 appearances in all competitions during seven successful years at Etihad Stadium.
As well as four Premier League titles, he helped City win five League Cups, one FA Cup and one Community Shield.
It was while he was at City, in 2021, that Sterling became an MBE in the Queen's Birthday Honours for his services to racial equality in sport.
"I am grateful to have been recognised," he said. "But my priority is to try to help to educate society and myself. I'm learning every day."
After City came the move to Chelsea , where his career began to stall.
Tuchel, now England manager, was sacked two months after signing Sterling, who made just 45 Premier League starts for the Blues over four years.
Off the pitch, he launched a scholarship fund aimed at closing the gap in the number of black British students who go to university.
He spent 18 months as a member of Chelsea 's so-called 'bomb squad' , and a season-long loan to Arsenal in 2024-25 proved largely unsuccessful.
Sterling: If you grew up in a certain area you feel like there's limits
As well as his success on the field, Sterling has made headlines off it too.
In 2015, when he was 20, reports began to surface about his behaviour away from the game.
Sterling was pictured apparently inhaling nitrous oxide and was also photographed smoking a shisha pipe.
That prompted then Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers to warn Sterling he would "look back in 20 years and wonder what he was doing".
Sterling also made headlines while on duty for England at the 2018 World Cup in Russia.
The Sun ran a story titled "Raheem shoots himself in the foot" as pictures emerged of a tattoo of an M16 assault rifle on his leg.
Sterling explained on social media: "When I was 2 my father died from being gunned down to death I made a promise to myself I would never touch a gun in my life time. I shoot with my right foot so it has a deeper meaning."
The incident led to a widespread discussion in the UK about the treatment of black athletes in the media, with comparisons drawn between how Sterling's life was covered compared to others.
Sterling spoke out a number of times on the issue and wider racism in society, which was reflected in him being made an MBE.
Five years after his MBE, Sterling's career has stalled. He has not played since appearing for Feyenoord on 17 May, after agreeing a short-term move to the Netherlands.
Eleven days after that game, he was arrested after crashing a Lamborghini near the M3 in Hampshire.
Listen: From Wembley schoolboy to playing for England at Wembley
Sterling was riding the crest of a wave when he moved from Manchester City to Chelsea in the summer of 2022 for £50m.
His medal cabinet was already fit to burst with 10 major trophies under Guardiola and, alongside Harry Kane, he was arguably England's most important player for then head coach Gareth Southgate.
Tuchel viewed Sterling as his number one target that summer and Chelsea 's new ownership - Behdad Eghbali and Todd Boehly - delivered as the club entered the post-Roman Abramovich era.
Two months later, Tuchel was sacked and Graham Potter was in situ.
It is, of course, senseless to suggest the troubles Sterling has had on and off the pitch in recent years are simply down to the sacking of Tuchel in 2022.
But speak to those close to Sterling and they will explain Tuchel was among the key factors behind the winger's decision to swap Manchester for west London.
He was captivated by Tuchel's vision, not only for the team, but his role in it.

Sporting Lisbon vs Manchester United. UEFA Champions League Round 1.
Report as Man Utd self-destruct in bizarre Champions League draw at Sporting after having two goals controversially ruled out; Bruno Fernandes and Luis Suarez both scored two goals, one penalty each, with the Man Utd captain's second goal freakishly bouncing in off a divot in the ground
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Mauricio Pochettino was denied a first victory as Manchester United head coach by a goalkeeping howler from Senne Lammens in an incident-packed 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League as Youri Tielemans was sent off late on.
United looked to be on course for a first away win of the season after captain Bruno Fernandes scored two goals in the first five minutes of the second half only for Lammens to spill the ball in the box for Luis Suarez to equalise with his second goal of the game.
Pochettino thought United had gone back in front for a second time shortly after Lammens' error when Sporting goalkeeper Kaique punched into his own net at a corner. However, it was ruled out following an on-field review for a foul by substitute Patrick Dorgu.
It was a damaging night for Lammens, who gave away the penalty for Suarez's first goal just 75 seconds after saving the Sporting striker's poorly taken spot-kick. The man brought into replace the error-prone Andre Onana is now beginning to resemble his predecessor.
Fernandes' equaliser three minutes after the restart came from the third penalty of what was a bizarre match. Few moments topped the United skipper's freakish second goal which came thanks a tame effort bouncing up off a divot in the ground and into back of the net.
Tielemans' stoppage-time red will only add to United's frustrations. It was his first booking, for a tame follow-through on Goncalo Inacio, that denied Amad Diallo from equalising late in the first half. "It is a terrible decision," said Sky Sports pundit Clinton Morrison.
Pochettino's first two matches have seen his side have two players sent off and concede two penalties. If he did not know it before, he certainly knows now that nothing comes easy at United, who sit 19th in the Champions League and Premier League.

Stoke City 2-1 Millwall: Potters beat Lions to make it five wins a in row
Bolton Wanderers 1-3 West Bromwich Albion: Aune Heggebo nets twice in Baggies win
Club Brugge 0-3 Liverpool: Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz on target in dominant Champions League win
Burnley 0-2 Birmingham City: August Priske nets as Blues ease past struggling Clarets
Rangers 3-2 Aberdeen: Gers beat Dons in five-goal thriller to cut Celtic's Premiership lead to one point
The last thing Pochettino needed after the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool - and Leny Yoro's now overturned red card - was more refereeing controversy. However, there was contention around both goals United had ruled out in Lisbon.
Amad had the ball in the back of the net toward the end of the first half to equalise - but not before the whistle had gone for what was judged to have been a foul by Tielemans, who clearly won the ball with his slide tackle.
The United midfielder received a booking for his follow through on Sporting defender Inacio, who went down dramatically despite receiving the slightest of contact. VAR could not intervene as the whistle had gone.
Morrison, who said Tielemans "won the ball", was adamant that it was the wrong call.
United's second disallowed goal, which was ruled out following VAR intervention, saw Dorgu penalised for making contact with Sporting goalkeeper Kaique before he punched into his own net.
Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher felt it was "very harsh" for the referee to disallow the goal after being sent to his monitor.
"I do think United were a little bit unlucky tonight with the goal disallowed just before half-time. The goal at the end felt very harsh to me, the one where it could have been 3-2...
"The focus on a Man Utd goalkeeper is always big if he's making mistakes. The back-ups aren't even at the level where you could say no matter how poorly the goalkeeper plays, you could change it. You worry about the confidence of that goalkeeper now.
"That mistake for the equaliser, the 2-2 goal, you say sometimes 'an amateur goalkeeper wouldn't make that mistake' and that just can't happen at this level."
"I'm so proud of the players. It was a tough game. I liked the team we played for 90 minutes, the personality, the character. It's difficult to find a game where you get punished in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions. Today we showed how we want to play after just one week of working together.
"We need to concentrate and focus more, try to recover better. The performance like today's is the best medicine to prepare for the next game."

Bayern Munich endured their first defeat of the season on Wednesday, losing 2-1 at Lille in the Champions League as a tough week for the German giants worsened.
Dayot Upamecano opened the scoring for Bayern but Ayase Ueda levelled for Lille before an Aleksandar Pavlovic own goal gifted the hosts victory. Bayern’s unbeaten record in all competitions was ended by a Lille side who kicked off in 35th place in the tournament’s league phase.
The defeat continued a terrible week for Bayern, who have lost star striker Harry Kane for several months to an ankle ligament injury on Friday and were also without Michael Olise due to a foot complaint. Teenage winger Lennart Karl was the only recognised forward in the visitors’ lineup, although Jamal Musiala and Luis Díaz came off the bench.
The centre-back Upamecano, a striker in his youth, had laughed off pre-game suggestions he could play up front. With 15 minutes gone, the Bayern defender channelled Kane when he rose highest to head in the opener from a Tom Bischof corner. Bayern controlled the first half, with little sign of the problems to come.
The visitors were fortunate when VAR intervened to disallow a Ueda goal early in the second half for a foul on Joshua Kimmich, but the Japan striker did get on the scoresheet after 62 minutes, guiding Nathan Ngoy’s pass into the bottom corner.
Lille were ahead just four minutes later when Pavlovic chopped an Ethan Mbappé shot into his own goal in comical fashion. The younger Mbappé broke through on the counter and scuffed his shot against the post, only for Pavlovic to bundle it into his own net.
Anthony Gordon scored twice as Barcelona cruised to a ⁠4-1 victory at Sabah , maintaining Hansi Flick’s ⁠side’s push for ⁠a ​top-eight finish with their fourth victory from five league-phase matches.
Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus ⁠also scored in the space of five second-half minutes for the Spanish champions, who are ⁠fourth in the 36-team league table, while the Azerbaijani debutants Sabah ​are 32nd.
Barcelona had been ‌frustrated for periods ‌in the first half before Adeyemi, filling in on ‌the right wing for the injured Lamine Yamal, delivered a cross that the goalkeeper, Stas Pokatilov, could only palm to the edge of the six-yard box and Gordon tapped home from close range.
Six minutes after the ‌restart, Pokatilov parried a Jesus effort straight into Gordon’s path and the England forward made no ​mistake. Adeyemi then scored himself in the 55th minute before Jesus added a fourth five minutes later. Sabah briefly lifted the crowd at ⁠the Baku Olympic Stadium when Joy-Lance Mickels found ​the net.
Donyell Malen’s penalty earned Roma a 2-2 draw away to Paris Saint-Germain , ending the injury-hit champions’ perfect record in this season’s tournament.
Malen stroked in from the spot in the 78th minute at the Parc des Princes, giving Gian Piero Gasperini’s side a welcome point after their collapse from two goals up to lose 3-2 at Manchester United last time out.
Roma took an early lead through Mario Hermoso, only for Illia Zabarnyi to head home from a PSG corner before substitute Ousmane Dembélé briefly put the hosts in front with a penalty of his own. The result halts a run of 12 consecutive wins in all competitions for Luis Enrique’s team, who sit second in the league table.
In Czechia, Villarreal earned their second win in five Champions League games thanks to Tajon Buchanan’s second-half winner against Slavia Prague . The Canada forward beat Jakub Markovic at his near post to secure a 1-0 win while the hosts were left to rue two major VAR interventions.
The Villarreal defender Renato Veiga was initially sent off for an elbow in the first half before it was downgraded to a yellow after a video review. Slavia had a late penalty overturned, too, after Pape Gueye’s challenge on Michal Sadilek was deemed not to be a foul after another look.
Elsewhere, Petar Sucic’s penalty set Internazionale on their way to a 2-0 home win over Stuttgart, Atlético Madrid saw off Norwegian side Viking by the same score, and Fenerbahce defeated nominal hosts Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0 at Stamford Bridge.

Newcastle United’s owner, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), is looking to sell up to 25% of the club by issuing new shares.
The New York-based bank JP Morgan, whose most recent involvement in a major football deal was Fifa’s aborted attempt to sell off 20% of its commercial rights last summer, has been appointed to handle the sale, as first reported by the Athletic .
PIF is seeking investment partners to help fund major infrastructure projects, such as building a new stadium or redeveloping St James’ Park, and would dilute its shareholding rather than profiting from the proceeds of the share issue.
The state-owned fund owns 84% of Newcastle after the departure of the minority shareholder Amanda Staveley two years ago, with the remaining 16% owned by the London-based Reuben brothers.
In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.
If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.
If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.
Newcastle are the second Premier League club to formally seek investment this season, after Everton’s owners appointed the US bank Moelis & Company to handle their sale process last month. Last summer Liverpool’s owner, Fenway Sports Group, sold 38% of the club to a consortium which includes the Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.
PIF sources insist it retains a long-term commitment to Newcastle, whose value has soared since it bought the club from Mike Ashley for £305m five years ago in a deal that has not proved as transformative for their fortunes as many expected.
Newcastle qualified for the Champions League twice under Eddie Howe, who also led the club to their first domestic trophy for 70 years by winning the Carabao Cup in 2025 , but the Premier League’s spending rules have prevented the owners from investing as heavily as the competition’s other state-owned club, Manchester City.
PIF has also cut back its spending on sport generally, with the Newcastle share issue coming months after the fund withdrew its support for LIV Golf , which filed for bankruptcy this month .
PIF has also sold a stake in the Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, is open to selling other clubs, and has withdrawn from a three-year deal to host the Women’s Tennis Association finals 12 months early.
Newcastle have been wrestling for several years with the issue of whether to expand St James’ Park or build a new stadium on an adjacent site, but have made clear a project on that scale would require external funding.

Raheem Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in September and admitted possession of six nitrous oxide cannisters for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Former England player Raheem Sterling has been given a suspended 12-month jail sentence for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the motorway.
Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in September to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on May 28. The sentence is suspended for 18 months.
He has also been handed a two-year driving ban and must undertake 100 hours of unpaid community work. Sterling will have to re-take a driving test to hold a licence.
The 31-year-old admitted possession of six nitrous oxide cannisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.
Mitigating factors taken into account by District Judge Kirsty Allman were Sterling's guilty plea, that he had no prior convictions and a clean driving licence prior to his arrest in May.
She also said she took into account Sterling's regret at his behaviour, attached great weight to testimonies about his character and the fact that, away from his footballing career and perhaps not in the public sphere, he is heavily involved with several charitable causes from the Raheem Sterling Foundation, the RS7 Academy and several charitable bursaries.
Further mitigation was that Sterling engaged with addiction services soon after his arrest in May and admitted himself into residential care for 12 days at an addiction centre, which the court saw as "genuine engagement".
The judge said Sterling was entirely culpable for the dangerous driving charge, saying: "You chose to drive, disregarding the safety of others".
Chief Inspector Chris Sharland from Hampshire Police said: "Nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas or NOS, is a Class C drug, and driving whilst under its influence is an emerging threat to the safety of motorists on our roads.
"Driving whilst impaired with nitrous oxide can cause unconsciousness, and in the worst-case scenarios neurological damage or death, so there is a very real risk of causing serious harm to yourself or other motorists.
"We urge drivers to be aware of not only the law, but the risk this type of behaviour carries - one decision can have devastating consequences."
Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate's side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020. He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.
Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019. He left for Chelsea in 2022 but after falling out of favour spent the 2024/25 season on loan at Arsenal.
Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the 2025/26 season. He is currently without a club.
In the 2021 Queen's Birthday Honours, Sterling was made an MBE for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out strongly against racism on and off the pitch for several years.
It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.
Sky Sports News' Geraint Hughes at Basingstoke Magistrates Court:
"When Raheem Sterling arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates Court for his sentencing, as you would expect he looked serious, but also quite anxious.
"He was wearing dark clothing and never once did his gaze do anything other than look forward or towards the judge inside the courtroom. You felt he was aware of the gravity of the situation and also - given that his legal team had told the court how ashamed he felt to be in this position and that he never ever wanted to be in front of a criminal court in his life again - you could sense that with his body language and his demeanour.
"When the district judge asked Raheem Sterling to stand while she delivered her sentence he did so at times looking downwards, but mainly straight at the judge, occasionally acknowledging her remarks.
"At the conclusion of her sentencing, when Sterling was told he was free to leave the court, there was no smile or any emotion. He just walked out of the courtroom with his legal team to whom he shook their hands and thanked them very quietly before being able to leave the court a free man having avoided a potential custodial sentence."

Covid-19 aşısıyla dünya çapında tanınan BioNTech'in kurucu ortakları Uğur Şahin ve Özlem Türeci, yeni girişimleri için büyük bir finansman turunun eşiğinde. Öne sürülen bilgilere göre çift, kanser tedavileri geliştirmek üzere kurdukları Arife adlı şirket için yaklaşık 1 milyar dolar toplamayı hedefliyor.
İddiaya göre Uğur Şahin ve Özlem Türeci, Avrupalı girişim sermayesi şirketi Plural'ın başını çektiği yatırımcı grubuyla masada. Taraflardan henüz resmi bir açıklama gelmezken, konuşulan anlaşmanın yalnızca doğrudan sermaye yatırımından oluşmadığı belirtiliyor.
Şirketin ismi ise 'Arife' olacak. Masadaki paket, Arife'ye yaklaşık 2,5 milyar dolar değer biçecek bir başlangıç yatırımının yanı sıra ileride şirket hissesine dönüştürülebilecek bir borç finansmanını da içeriyor. Hisseye dönüştürülebilir borç, girişim dünyasında özellikle hızlı büyümesi beklenen şirketlerde sıkça başvurulan bir yöntem olarak biliniyor.
Yeni şirketin odağında, BioNTech'in pandemi döneminde geliştirdiği aşıda kullanılan mRNA teknolojisi yer alıyor. Arife, bu altyapıdan yararlanarak yeni nesil kanser tedavileri üzerinde çalışacak.
Aslında bu hedef, ikilinin yıllardır peşinden koştuğu bir hayal. Şahin ve Türeci, BioNTech'i 2008 yılında mRNA tabanlı kanser tedavileri geliştirmek amacıyla kurmuştu. Ancak şirketin adını tüm dünyaya duyuran gelişme, ABD 'li ilaç devi Pfizer ile birlikte geliştirilen ve onay alan ilk mRNA aşısı olan Kovid-19 aşısı oldu.
Mainz merkezli şirket, pandeminin ardından da kanser alanındaki çalışmalarını sürdürmüş; bireyselleştirilmiş mRNA aşısı adayı BNT122 ile kolorektal kanser hastalarında Faz 2 denemelerine başlamıştı. Uğur Şahin de daha önce yaptığı değerlendirmelerde, ilk mRNA tabanlı kanser aşılarının 2030'dan önce onay almasını beklediğini dile getirmişti.
BioNTech'in CEO'su Uğur Şahin ve tıbbi direktörü Özlem Türeci, mart ayında yaptıkları açıklamayla şirketteki yönetim görevlerinden yıl sonunda ayrılacaklarını duyurmuştu. Çift, bu kararı yeni girişimlerine tüm enerjileriyle odaklanabilmek için aldıklarını açıklamıştı. Şirketin denetim kurulu da ikilinin yerine geçecek isimleri belirlemek için arayış başlatmıştı.
Yeni şirketin adı ise daha önce Arife olarak duyurulmuştu. Türkçede bayramdan önceki günü anlatan kelimeyle aynı adı taşıyan şirketin, finansman turunun tamamlanmasıyla birlikte çalışmalarını hızlandırması bekleniyor.

Oyuncu Hazar Ergüçlü, 19 yıldır psikolojik destek aldığını açıkladı. Yeni filmi Mutter: Bir Annenin Hatıra Defteri için verdiği röportajda mesleğinin psikolojik açıdan zorlayıcı yönlerine değinen Ergüçlü, oyunculuk sektöründeki belirsizlik ve rekabetin baş etmesi güç duygular yarattığını söyledi.
T24'te yayımlanan ve Alphan Eşeli'nin de katıldığı röportajda Ergüçlü'ye, filmin gösteriminin ardından bir izleyicinin yönelttiği “Hazar Ergüçlü bu filmden sonra psikolojik destek almış mıdır?” sorusu hatırlatıldı.
Bu soruya yanıt veren oyuncu, “Vallahi ben zaten 19 yıldır psikolojik destek alıyorum. Oyuncunun alması gerekiyor zaten, kaçınılmaz” ifadelerini kullandı.
Oyunculuk mesleğinin beraberinde getirdiği zorluklara dikkat çeken Ergüçlü, özellikle belirsizlik ve rekabetin psikolojik açıdan zorlayıcı olduğunu belirtti.
Ergüçlü, “Bizim mesleğimizdeki bu belirsizlik her zaman olan tek bir şey. Rekabet çok zorlayıcı. Bunların karşısında gerçekten çelik gibi sinirlerinin olması gerekiyor” dedi.
Oynadığı rollerin yarattığı duygusal yükün de zaman zaman bu sürece eklendiğini anlatan Ergüçlü, karakterlerle kurduğu ilişkiyi anlattı.
Oyuncu, “Oynadığın rolün gerilimi ve yarattığı problemler bazen ekleniyor. Ama sonuçta o bir karakter. Ben bildiğim yerden bir takım ortak duyguları araştırarak onu kendime yaklaştırıyorum. Ben olsam ne yapardım diye yaklaşmaya çalışıyorum” ifadelerini kullandı.
Psikolojik desteğin yalnızca rol sürecinden kaynaklanmadığını vurgulayan Ergüçlü, sözlerini şöyle tamamladı:
“Rol ve oyunculuk, yani oyun anı psikolojik desteği en az gerektiren kısmı. Arkası daha fena. Oyunculuk kısmı kolay maalesef.”

Maçtan önce anlatınca Polyanna oluyorum, ben gerçekleri söylüyorum, oyuncularımla ne yaşadığımı söylüyorum. U21, U20 seviyelerindeler. Öğrenmeleri gereken birçok iş var. Biz bu mağlubiyetleri yönetecek cesaretteyiz.
İyi oynamadık. Bu kadar top kaybına can dayanmaz. Bazen futbol böyle. Bu mağlubiyetten ders çıkaracağız. Gelişmeye devam edeceğiz. Elimizde ne olduğunu biliyoruz, gençler ve potansiyelliler, doğrumuzdan vazgeçmeyeceğiz.
Bu şekilde kazanamazsın. Anları doğru oynasak belki puan alabilirdik. Pes etmeyeceğiz. Bizim için üzücü bir durum. Şartları biliyoruz. Saha içi performans yetmez. Üzüntülüyüz. Mağlubiyet, futbolcunun cehennemi. Bu cehennemi yaşayacağız. Ayağa kalkacağız."
Shakhtar Donetsk'in ligdeki durumuna ve Şampiyonlar Ligi seviyesine değinen Turan, organizasyonda tecrübe kazanmanın önemini vurguladı.
Arda Turan, " Ligde iyiyiz, tepedeyiz. Ukrayna'ya, Dinamo Kiev'e bakın, gruplara dahi gelemediler. Çok zor. Şampiyonlar Ligi'ni öğrenmek lazım. Oyuncularım yetenekli mi çok yetenekli ama yetenek bu oyunun sadece bir parçası. Bir şeylere geç kalıyoruz. Şampiyonlar Ligi'nde bizim için bir anı olarak güzel, ders çıkarmam gereken bir durum. Bakacağız. Çok üzüntülüyüz " dedi.
Arda Turan, Fenerbahçe Teknik Direktörü Emre Belözoğlu'na da tebriklerini iletti.
Genç hoca, " Emre Ağabey adına tüm kalbimle tebriklerimi iletiyorum, gönülden sarılıyorum ona. Bundan sonrası için başarılar diliyorum " ifadelerini kullandı.
